newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Tap Oil shares sparked by Woollybutt data.
newsitem.headline: Tap Oil shares sparked by Woollybutt data.

text.p: Shares in oil and gas explorer Tap Oil NL leapt over 13 percent to an intraday high of A$1.37 on Monday after promising drilling results from its offshore West Australia Woollybutt One exploration well.
The company said the well was likely to contain a gross hydrocarbon column of betweeen 11 and 17 metres.
"It's up on the results this morning," said a Sydney based dealer, adding that there was still very healthy demand for the emerging oil and gas players.

"The market has made an extraordinary amount of money out of the oil sector in recent times, especially the developing stocks like Tap Oil, and when they come out with good results the market has a real appetite for them."

Tap Oil has a 10 percent stake in the well, which is operated by 20 percent owner Mobil Exploration & Producing Australia Pty Ltd. Pan Canadian Petroleum International Ltd has 40 percent and Hardy Petroleum Ltd 30 percent.
By 1.30 p.m. (0330 GMT), Tap Oil shares were 12 cents higher at A$1.33 on turnover of 1.3 million shares.
